text: 🇲🇽✊ "They said that if the minimum wage went up there would be inflation. False." "The minimum wage went up and the peso is strong. The minimum wage went up and we are at a record of foreign direct investment." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Puebla The minimum wage went from 2,800 pesos a month in 2018 to more than 9,500 in 2026 — a 154% real increase. Outsourcing was banned, digital platform workers gained social security, and the workweek will drop two hours a year to reach 40 hours in 2030.
banner: MINIMUM WAGE UP 154% IN REAL TERMS

text: 🇲🇽✊ "It is love made public policy." "Do you know how many people in Puebla receive well-being programs? 2,165,549 people… It is the people's taxes returned to the people of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Puebla In Puebla: 667,000 older adults receive the universal pension, 104,000 people with disabilities a pension, and 228,234 high-school students a Benito Juárez scholarship. Also underway: 812 new IMSS-Bienestar doctor's offices, about 18 new high schools, some 69,000 well-being homes, and around 20 treatment plants to clean up the Atoyac, the country's most polluted river.

🇲🇽📜 "Only the people of Mexico can define their destiny — no foreign power, no elite can define the destiny of the homeland." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Honesty and Results, Puebla She was explaining Article 39 of the Constitution — national sovereignty resides in the people — which traces back to Morelos' 1814 Constitution. She also recalled Morelos' call to "moderate indigence and opulence" and his demand that the son of the hacendado and the son of the peon receive the same education: "the defense of public education, ever since."
banner: "ONLY THE PEOPLE CAN DEFINE ITS DESTINY"

text: 🇲🇽🏭 "If you orient a development program by missions and organize the government so that all of us are there to fulfill those missions, it will advance faster." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, on meeting economist Mariana Mazzucato Mazzucato analyzed how the government could reorganize around Plan México's goals, citing the Apollo program as a model. Sheinbaum pointed to the 1.8-million-home housing program as a driver of innovation in concrete, solar water heaters and new materials. On patents from public research: "Whoever should receive the largest royalty is the public institution, because public resources were used."

🇲🇽💻 "What is made with public money is public." "Digitalization is building public capacities, technological sovereignty and, of course, savings, austerity." — José Antonio Peña Merino, head of the Digital Transformation Agency The government's in-house software factory — 300 Mexican engineers — built 279 systems, work that would have cost 14 billion pesos if contracted out. The public data center in Aguascalientes already hosts 450 government systems, with a second planned in Tulancingo. Code is shared with states and municipalities through a National Public Technology Repository.

🚨🇲🇽 "They could not be carrying out these activities in our country without the permission of Foreign Affairs." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera Diario 24 Horas reported that the US government hired four companies to come to Mexico and notify deported Mexicans of immigration fines they owe in the United States. Sheinbaum said the US Embassy has not confirmed the report, and that no such operation can take place in Mexico without authorization from the Foreign Ministry (SRE).
banner: US FINE COLLECTORS NEED SRE PERMIT

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "My grandfather was a Juarista and my father a Zapatista." "And I sow on someone else's land, even though I'm an agrarista." — Amparo Ochoa, honored in the mañanera's Women in History segment Born in Sinaloa in 1946, the rural teacher became one of Mexico's most combative voices of the Nueva Canción. She sang of the Revolution and national sovereignty, recorded in solidarity with the Chilean people after the 1973 coup, and took up the cause of Mexican migrants and the Chicano movement in the US. Her songs include "El Barzón", "La Adelita" and "El otro México". She died in 1994; September 29 marks 80 years since her birth.

🇲🇽📈 Mexico's economy grew 3.3% year-on-year in July. "I told you we would keep advancing in economic growth, in the second half, and in 2027… The industrial sector also grew, not only services." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum INEGI's IGAE activity index for July 2026: +3.3% versus July 2025 and +0.8% versus June, with World Cup tourism lifting services. INEGI's self-reported well-being module puts average life satisfaction in Mexico at 8.83 out of 10.
